cards.questionText:
Books by James Trozelli 

The History of Jeans 

Where did it all begin? Troxelli visually chronicles the evolution of jeans through the centuries ,from working wear to high fashion. Who knew that jeans would become one of the most popular garments in countries around the world?

Look Past the Runway 

Trozelli captures the creative process of some of the top designers from New York City to Paris. Spanning almost twenty years, the book is filled with Trozelli's photographs and shows what goes on in fashion houses before designs are ready for the runway. 

Growing Into Clothes: My Story 

An amusing memoir about growing up in the fashion world. Trozelli writes about his unconventional upbringing in New York City with parents who began as fashion models before launching their own design label.

 Yards of Talent: A Decade of Style 

 A collection of Trozelli's images spanning a decade of fashion and revealing what was in style, what was out of style, and then what was back in style again. The book offers a sweeping array of some of the top trends in fashion.

To: listenercomments @btwradio.com

From: cogilvie@sunmail.net

Date: September 24

Subject: Radio Interview 

I discovered BTW Radio over 20 years ago and have been a regular listener of your evening programming for at least a decade. I just want to say how much I enjoy your newest offering. I've been interested in many of the authors that have been featured on the show so far, but last evening's guest was especially entertaining. 

I remember James from when he was a little boy. I worked with his parents when they lived in New York, and I recall seeing James in his parents' studio most days after he got out of school. I was surprised to learn that he has written about his childhood, and I look forward to reading his new book. 

Thank you for the excellent program. 

Calista Ogilvie

cards.questionText:
Attention Everyone: Group Photo This Saturday

Exciting news - Tasty Bites Magazine will be featuring our restaurant in an article about Dublin's best dining establishments! They have arranged for one of their photographers to photograph us on Saturday, 4 June, at 10:00 A.M., before preparations for the day begin. 

All employees will be included, so please plan to come in a bit sooner than scheduled on Saturday morning wearing your uniform. The session will take 30 minutes. 

We have achieved so much since we opened, and you should all be very proud of this recognition.

To: Herman Keel <hkeel @bentonsidebistro.net>

From: Hilary Seaton <hseaton@hbsphotography.com>

Date: Wednesday, 1 June

Subject: Saturday Photography Appointment 

Dear Mr. Keel, 

I am writing to confirm your group photography session at 10:00 A.M. on Saturday. As discussed, this photo shoot will take place at your restaurant, and I will photograph your staff along the wall in the main dining hall. You mentioned that your waitstaff will need to start getting ready for the day at 10:30 A.M., and that should not be a problem. The shoot should be finished by 10:30 A.M ..

 Please let me know if you have any questions. Otherwise, I will see you on Saturday! 

Hilary Seaton 

HBS Photography

BISTRO

Enter Bentonside Bistro any day for lunch or dinner, and you'll hear the sounds of clinking forks and chattering patrons. “That's the sound of happy diners,”  says Herman Keel, the restaurant's owner. 

Opened two years ago, the bistro has exceeded expectations. The menu features traditional Irish dishes prepared by chef Deirdre Hanrahan. She notes, "We choose ingredients that are at the height of summer, fall, winter, and spring, and showcase these on our menu."

 On a recent Wednesday afternoon, Jacinta Coelho, a visitor from Brazil, was dining at the bistro. "I can't get over the freshness and homemade taste!" exclaimed Ms. Coelho. “It's like the chef  went outside and selected the ingredients just for me.”

Bentonside Bistro is located at 1644 Bentonside Road and is open Tuesday through Saturday from 11:30 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. The interior is painted in bright shades of blue reminiscent of the ocean, with a rotating gallery of artwork adorning the walls. The staff is friendly and the delicious food is reasonably priced. Reservations are not required. 

By Declan Mulroney, Staff Writer

Delta City Art Museum – Current Exhibitions

The Impressionists (May 1–June 30, Main Gallery)
This exhibition presents paintings from the renowned nineteenth-century Impressionist movement, featuring works by both celebrated and lesser-known artists.

Native American Pottery (May 15–July 16, Shawe Memorial Gallery)
Visitors can explore the diverse pottery-making methods and traditions created and practiced by Indigenous communities throughout North America.

Classical Greece and Beyond (May 22–August 21, Techtmann Gallery)
The exhibition displays sculptures of human figures from ancient Greece alongside contemporary artworks inspired by classical Greek aesthetics.

Artists of Delta City (Permanent Exhibition, Zhang Atrium)
This well-attended exhibition highlights modern creations by local artists across a variety of mediums, such as oil and watercolor paintings, photography, fiber arts, and mixed-media pieces. While the exhibition remains on display year-round, the featured artworks are rotated regularly and are available for viewing only for limited periods.

To:         Delta City Art Museum info@deltacityartmuseum.org

From:     Lorelei Desnoyers lorelei.desnoyers@klarsenuniversity.edu

Date:      May 2

Subject: Request for Information

Good morning,

I recently joined Klarsen University as an art instructor. A fellow faculty member informed me that the Delta City Art Museum offers guided visits for local art students. I would like to arrange a visit for my Art 103 class so that students can observe and sketch some of the artworks currently exhibited.

Because the course emphasizes the study and drawing of the human figure, we will primarily focus on the museum’s sculptures. Nevertheless, I would appreciate the opportunity for the class to take a short guided tour of the entire museum before beginning our sketching activities.

Please let me know whether such an arrangement would be possible.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,

Lorelei Desnoyers

School of Art & Design

Klarsen University

504-555-0177

To:         Lorelei Desnoyers lorelei.desnoyers@klarsenuniversity.edu

From:    Jocelyn Grady jgrady@deltacityartmuseum.org

Date:     May 3

Subject: RE: Inquiry

Dear Ms. Desnoyers,

Thank you for reaching out. Your colleague was right - the museum does offer guided tours for local art students. We would most likely arrange your visit on a Tuesday, as it is generally the quietest day of the week. I have passed your inquiry along to our Public Programs Office, and a member of the team will contact you by phone to provide additional information.

Please be aware that paints of any kind, including watercolors, are not allowed inside the museum galleries. However, visitors may use pencils and charcoal, provided they are careful not to mark or smudge any museum property. Photography and video recording are also permitted, as long as they do not disturb other guests.

Thank you for your interest in the Delta City Art Museum. We look forward to welcoming you and your students.

Best regards,

Jocelyn Grady

Information and Community Outreach

Delta City Art Museum
